reviews.head: Rock Nut Tasting Menu, Seven Courses
reviews.body: Course one was a rock nut. Course two was a rock nut, warmer. By course five the chef was visibly running out of ideas and simply placed the bag on the table. Texture: geological. The paste course was bold, in that it was also a rock nut.

reviews.head: Quarry Bush Leaves, Lightly Dressed
reviews.body: The menu calls them 'leaves'. I call them 'what the farmer found'. Crunchy, bitter, faintly accusing. A worthy side dish for anyone who has wronged the kitchen. I have apparently wronged the kitchen.

reviews.head: The Fine Meal, Ingredients Unlisted
reviews.body: The waiter described it as 'a fine stew of dwarven syrup, cave lobster and a third thing'. I asked about the third thing. He said the cook also asked about the third thing. Delicious, with an aftertaste of questions.

reviews.head: Dimple Cup Gala Dinner
reviews.body: Every dish at this gala was dyed blue, including the bread, the cheese and, for a brief moment, the host. Flavour unremarkable. Colour unforgettable. I left with a blue beard and a deep sense of occasion.

reviews.head: 'Job Cancelled: Interrupted', a Farce
reviews.body: A dwarf sets out to haul a mug. He is interrupted by a cat. He sets out again. A different cat. Ninety minutes, eleven cats, zero mugs. The audience wept with recognition. The mug, I understand, is still on the floor.

reviews.head: 'Unmemorialised', a Ghost Story Matinee
reviews.body: The ghost in the lead role was a genuine ghost who wandered on stage looking for a slab. The cast improvised around her bravely. Three understudies fainted. She received a standing ovation and, afterwards, a slab. Best ending this season.

reviews.head: 'The Liaison Asks About Trade', a Monologue
reviews.body: One actor, one chair, two hours of asking whether we would like to discuss the trade agreement. We would not. He asks again. The final act, in which he leaves until next year, drew the loudest cheer I have ever heard.

reviews.head: 'Up, Then Down, Then Up', a Poem on Ramps
reviews.body: A bold experiment: every line of this poem climbs one z-level, then descends. Readers on the lower floors reported missing the middle stanza entirely. I read it standing on a ramp and frankly felt very moved, mostly upward.

reviews.head: Mandate Haiku, Collected
reviews.body: Seventeen syllables per mandate, eighteen if the noble insisted. Highlight: 'Make three gold goblets / I do not need three goblets / I need you to try.' The collection ends with a haiku banning haiku. Seems fair.

reviews.head: 'Ballad of {masterwright}', by an Admirer
reviews.body: Thirty stanzas praising {masterwright}'s recent work, each rhyming 'masterpiece' with 'piece' and then, with growing desperation, 'geese'. The sentiment is real. The geese are not explained. Recommended to the subject's mother.

reviews.head: 'A Codex on Doors, With Some Remarks on Hatches'
reviews.body: A thorough treatment. The author has opened every door in the fortress and closed most of them. The chapter on forbidden doors is gripping. The appendix on hatches is for specialists. I finished it and immediately locked myself in.

reviews.head: 'Momentum, and Other Regrets', a Quire
reviews.body: Written in the hospital by a former minecart enthusiast, this short work explains track physics in plain language: things go fast, then they stop, then you are in the hospital. Diagrams drawn left-handed for reasons made clear in chapter one.

reviews.head: 'Every Dwarf Called Urist', a Scroll
reviews.body: Exhaustive. Literally exhausting. The scroll unrolled across the dining hall, through the kitchen and into the tavern, where it was used as a tablecloth. Scholars call it definitive. Everyone else calls it the tablecloth.

reviews.head: Drum Recital During the Siege
reviews.body: The drummer played straight through the goblin assault and never once lost the beat, chiefly because he was locked behind the drawbridge with nowhere else to be. Tempo: brisk. Encore: involuntary. Siege: unaffected.

reviews.head: Premiere of a New Musical Form
reviews.body: The composer explained the form for forty minutes: one melody, played on a lyre, then interrupted by a second lyre that disagrees. The performance itself lasted nine seconds. The explanation was better. I would attend the explanation again.

reviews.head: Migrant Shanties at the Gate
reviews.body: Newcomers sang the long songs of the road, about walking, then walking, then a hill. The fortress joined in on the chorus, which was simply 'are we there yet'. Rousing stuff. Nobody had the heart to tell them the beds are not built.

reviews.head: The Smoothed Corridor, East Wing
reviews.body: Smooth as a cheese and nearly as tempting to lick, which I am told several apprentices have done. The engraver has not yet arrived, leaving the walls in a state of pure promise. A corridor at the height of its potential.

reviews.head: The Statue Garden, Level Four
reviews.body: Forty statues in one room, every one of them depicting a dwarf looking at another statue. The effect is recursive and deeply unsettling. Excellent for raising room value. Terrible for anyone who wants to be alone with their thoughts.

reviews.head: The Great Up/Down Staircase
reviews.body: One hundred and four levels of straight stair, top to bottom, no landings, no railings, no mercy. A triumph of ambition over knees. I climbed it once for this review. I am writing it from the hospital, where the view is worse.

reviews.head: The Spiked Band, Menacing with Bone
reviews.body: This season's must-have bracelet is encircled with bands of menacing spikes, menacing with spikes, and menacing in general. Wearers report excellent respect at the dining table and great difficulty scratching their noses.

reviews.head: The Militia's New Uniform, Partially Worn
reviews.body: Someone ticked 'replace clothing' on the uniform order and the entire squad paraded in steel helms, breastplates and nothing else. Bold, breezy, historically unprecedented. The goblins retreated immediately. Five stars for tactics, one for modesty.

reviews.head: Pig Tail Fibre Tunics
reviews.body: Made from the plant, not the pig, as the clothier has explained to every single customer. Soft, durable, breathable, and impossible to wear without someone asking about the pig. Fashion should start conversations. This one never ends.

reviews.head: The Tavern, Visitor Night
reviews.body: Packed with travelling performers, a poet, two bards and a monster slayer who wanted a job. Nobody bought a drink; everyone asked for residency. The keeper served a single mug to forty petitioners. Atmosphere: hopeful. Profits: hypothetical.

reviews.head: The Snug Behind the Still, {drinks} in Stock
reviews.body: With {drinks} drinks in the barrels, the snug has the warm glow of a place that will not run dry this week. The seats are barrels. The barrels are full. Customers keep checking. Every check is a joy.

reviews.head: The Tavern, Snowed In
reviews.body: The surface entrance is buried, which the regulars consider a feature. Nobody new can get in, nobody old wants to leave, and the fire is stoked with old furniture of questionable sentimental value. Cozy, smoky, slightly illegal.

reviews.head: Picnic in the First Cavern
reviews.body: Lovely fungus trees, soft moss, a gentle drip. Lunch was interrupted by a giant cave toad who joined us uninvited and ate the cheese, the basket and some of the blanket. He was a better guest than my cousin. Four stars, one for the toad.

voxpops.q: Did you pull the lever?
answers: No. Which lever? No.
I pulled a lever. Not THE lever. A lever.
The lever pulled me, if anything.
I was in the tavern with eleven witnesses, all asleep.
Was it the one that floods things? Then no.
I'm a mechanic. I don't pull them. I just make them irresistible.

voxpops.q: Is there a vampire in {fort}?
answers: Absolutely not, said the bookkeeper who has not slept in nine years.
If there is, I hope they can haul.
I've never seen anyone not drink. That's the problem.
There was a pale dwarf in the hall, but that was just my cousin after the surface.
I sleep with a clove of garlic. We don't grow garlic. I sleep with an onion-shaped rock.
Leave him alone, he's a lovely dwarf. Very thirsty.

voxpops.q: What did you tell the liaison?
answers: That I was a statue. He believed me for an hour.
I said 'trade' and ran.
He asked about the trade agreement. I asked about his hat. We both left unsatisfied.
I gave him a mug. He wrote it down as a treaty.
He asked if we had any complaints. I gave him the list. He's still reading it.
Nothing. I've been in the latrine since he arrived. It's lovely in here.

voxpops.q: What did you see during the strange mood?
answers: {moodname} locked the door and screamed for shells. We don't have shells.
A blur. A hammer. A sudden, beautiful {artifact_item}.
I handed over a bone and was thanked in a language I'd never heard.
Honestly it looked like a normal workday, but louder.
I'd like my leather back.
The door opened, the artifact came out, and {moodname} asked what day it was.

voxpops.q: What did you think when we broke into the caverns?
answers: That there should've been a door there.
Mostly 'run'.
The moss is lovely. The things standing on it are not.
I thought: more room for beds. Then I saw the crundles.
I was the miner. I'm still thinking it.
Finally, somewhere with a ceiling high enough for my hat.

voxpops.q: What's life like in the militia?
answers: Up at dawn, punch a dummy, nap. Honestly great.
My uniform is a helmet and an optimistic attitude.
We spar, we bleed, we tell each other we're improving.
The captain says I'm a natural. A natural what, he won't say.
I trained with a crossbow for a year. I hit things with it. Not with bolts. With it.
The danger room has taught me many things, mainly to walk faster.

voxpops.q: What's your favourite engraving in the fort?
answers: The one of the dwarf and the cheese. The cheese is laughing.
The image of the fortress being founded. I'm in it, looking surprised.
The one of an elf being struck down. Very soothing.
The image of a ring. Just a ring. It's art.
The one in my bedroom. It's of my bedroom.
There's one of the cat. The cat looks at it. I worry about the cat.

voxpops.q: Where in the fort do you feel most at home?
answers: Anywhere with a barrel at arm's length.
The forge. It's warm, it's loud, nobody asks questions.
The bottom of the up/down stairs, recovering.
The library. Not to read. To nap without being hauled.
Next to the magma. My mother said I was born for it. I think she meant something else.
The refuse pile. Don't judge me. It's quiet.

voxpops.q: Did you see the thief?
answers: I saw a goblet walk out of the depot. I assumed it had somewhere to be.
Small, green, holding my bracelet, waving.
No, but my dog did, and he's still barking about it.
The thief was very polite. He said 'excuse me' on the way out.
I saw nothing. I was guarding the gate.
Yes, and I'd like to formally apologise for waving back.

voxpops.q: What's the best thing you ever traded for?
answers: A barrel of exotic syrup. The barrel was nicer than the syrup.
A pet I can't name. It eats rope.
Three socks. Not a pair. Three. I'm living my truth.
An elven song. I paid in tables. Worth it, don't tell anyone.
A human hat. It has a brim. I can't see anything. I love it.
My cousin, back. They'd sold him. Long story.

voxpops.q: What do you do when the river freezes?
answers: Walk on it, nervously.
Bring a pick and make a well. Lose the pick. Make another well.
Slide. Then hospital.
Write a strongly worded letter to the river.
Sit in the tavern pretending rivers don't exist.
Last year I got frozen in it to my knees. Lovely view.

voxpops.q: How do you feel about the caged goblin?
answers: He's alright. He's got opinions about masonry.
I feed him on Tuesdays. He's a picky eater for a goblin.
We play cards. He cheats. I cheat back. It's fair.
He's been here longer than half the migrants and complains less.
He hums. Nicely. He taught me a goblin lullaby. Every verse is about spears. It's weirdly soothing.
The cage is nicer than my room, frankly.

voxpops.q: Who do you pray to, and how's it going?
answers: The god of rivers and boredom. Very responsive.
Mostly to whoever keeps the barrels full.
I pray at the temple, the dining hall and occasionally to my pick.
I haven't been able to pray in a year. I'm told my god has moved on.
Our deity of fire and cheese is generous with both.
I prayed for a better bedroom. I got a better bed. Close enough.

voxpops.q: What do you think of the new noble?
answers: He walks into rooms like he owns them. He does own some of them.
He's demanded a throne. We gave him a stool with ambition.
He made a mandate for crowns. I'm a fish cleaner.
Pleasant enough when he's asleep.
His hat has its own bedroom now.
I like him. He's nice to the cats. He's not nice to anyone else.

voxpops.q: If you could adopt any animal, which?
answers: A {topanimal}, obviously, there are {topanimal_n} of them and they need homes.
A giant cave toad. Low maintenance, high presence.
An elephant. I've heard stories. I want to be the story.
A cat, but a well-behaved one, if such exists.
A forgotten beast, a small one. A starter beast.
The goblin's cage pet. We've grown close.

voxpops.q: Sweet pod syrup: overrated or underrated?
answers: Underrated. I put it on everything, including other syrup.
It's sticky. I'm still sticky from last spring.
My grandfather was a syrup maker. He was mostly sticky, mostly happy.
Overrated. Rock nut paste is the true condiment.
I've never had it. It's always 'for the cook'.
It's delicious, and also the strongest glue in the fort.

voxpops.q: What's the first thing you do in {season}?
answers: Ask someone what {season} is like up top.
Change socks. Annually.
Check the barrels. Same as every season.
Reposition my bed slightly to the left. Ritual.
Haul. Everything. All of it. That's every season, actually.
Write the date on the wall so I know how long I've been down here.

voxpops.q: How do you feel about the drawbridge?
answers: I respect it. It doesn't respect me.
I stood on it once when it was raised. I'll describe the trip when I'm well.
It's our best defender. It's killed more goblins than the militia.
It's a door that thinks it's a wall.
I wave to it every morning. Something about it seems lonely.
Please stop asking. My cousin was in its way.

voxpops.q: What woke you up last night?
answers: A cat walking across my face. Standard.
The forge. Someone works nights for no reason.
A distant scream. Possibly singing. Possibly joyful.
The ghost, again. It wanted me to know the slab was crooked.
My own snoring. It echoes off the smoothed walls.
The drawbridge. Who raises a drawbridge at midnight? Rhetorical.

voxpops.q: What's the first thing a baby in {fort} should learn?
answers: Where the barrels are.
How to dodge mugs during tantrums.
Never touch the lever.
That the sky is a rumour and should stay that way.
To haul. Start them early. They've got good grip.
How to tell a cat from a cat-shaped trap.

help_wanted.text: LEVER PULLER: Wait by the lever. Pull only when told. You will never be told. Excellent opportunity for patient, curious dwarves who can resist anything except levers.
WANTED: Dwarf to feed the caged goblin. He bites, but only out of habit. Must not answer when he asks to 'just open it a bit'.
DYER sought. Dimple cups provided. Every item in the fort is currently beige, including the moods. Bring colour, bring hope, bring a bucket.
SPINNER needed. We have {thread} thread and twice as many requests for trousers. Spinning wheel provided. Spare finger insurance not.
GHOST LIAISON: Listen to ghost complaints, write them down, arrange slabs. Night shift. Hazard pay in candles. Previous liaison is now a client.
WELL DIGGER needed. Must dig straight down until water appears. Must stop digging when water appears. Second part is where previous applicants struggled.
ART CRITIC: Walk the corridors and describe each engraving aloud. Our last critic described one as 'a dwarf, and a dwarf'. He was correct. We want more than correct.
CAGE TRAP INSPECTOR: Check that each cage trap is armed. Our last inspector checked by walking. He is in cage number four. He reports it works.
SCRIBE wanted to copy books for the library. Original books are mostly about rocks. Copies may be about anything you like, as long as nobody checks.
DEPOT GUARD: Watch the merchants. Watch the thieves. If the merchants are the thieves, watch both, and please send a note to the broker.
PRESSER needed for sweet pods. Fruit provided. Sticky fingers guaranteed. Sticky everything guaranteed. We have stopped trying to un-stick the press.
MANDATE READER: Read the noble's demands aloud to the workshops, then soften the bad news. Must be able to say 'crowns, again' without sighing.
TEMPORARY: Someone to guard the cheese while the chef sleeps. The cheese has been taken three nights running. The chef suspects himself.
WANTED: Two strong dwarves to relieve the pump operators, who have not stopped since spring and have begun to hum in perfect unison. Urgent. Spooky.
SURVEYOR for the first cavern. Draw a map, note the toads, flee from the rest. Map need not be accurate, just not on fire.
CENSUS TAKER: {pop} dwarves, probably. Count them. Then count them again, since they keep moving. Cats do not count, no matter what they claim.
WANTED: Whoever took all the crutches. You aren't in trouble. The hospital just needs them back for the dwarves who are in trouble.
BEEKEEPER wanted. Hives provided. Bees provided. Bees not consulted. Honey highly probable, swelling very probable.
SOAP MAKER needed. We have lye, we have tallow, we have a fort that smells like a fort. Please hurry. Please.
BRIDGE ATTENDANT: Warn dwarves standing on the drawbridge before it rises. Shout clearly. Shout early. Shout again. Shouting skills a must.
WOOD BURNER: Turn {wood} logs into charcoal before the elves find out and send a letter. Quiet work. Very warm. Smells of guilt.
HUNTER sought. Desperately. The fort hasn't seen meat since the founding, and someone has started carving cheese into steak shapes. Please help.
EMERGENCY BREWER: The barrels are low. The dwarves are lower. Do not walk past the tavern without a mug in each hand and an excuse in your mouth.
SHEARER for our {herd} head of livestock. Wool is useful. Animals disagree. Bring shears, patience, and a willingness to be chased round the pasture.
TUTOR needed for the children of {fort}. Subjects: reading, counting, not touching levers. The children already know the third one, theoretically.

real_estate.head: Quiet Crypt, Night Owl Preferred
real_estate.text: Ideal for residents who sleep all day and drink something other than wine. Previous tenant moved out suddenly after the sheriff 'asked a few questions'. Excellent soundproofing.

real_estate.head: Former Goblin Cage, Spacious
real_estate.text: Bars on every side for excellent airflow. Comes with a view of the depot and the goblin who used to live here, now just next door. He's quiet. Mostly.

real_estate.head: Studio Overlooking the Artifact Pedestal
real_estate.text: Wake up to a view of {artifact}. Walk past it. Walk past it again. Rumours of mood-induced envy are exaggerated. Tenants may not touch the artifact.

real_estate.head: Cottage on a Ramp
real_estate.text: Floors at three different heights, with charm at all of them. Furniture slides gently east over time. Ideal for dwarves who enjoy waking up somewhere slightly new.

real_estate.head: Temple Annex, Prayer-Adjacent
real_estate.text: Live where you pray. Pray where you live. Neighbours are pious, loud and very early. Includes complimentary sermon through the wall.

real_estate.head: Fully Smoothed Bedroom
real_estate.text: Walls smooth as river glass. Floors smooth as cheese. Engraver booked for next year, possibly. Mirror-quality surfaces; tenants with unflattering beards be warned.

real_estate.head: Bedroom Above the Cistern
real_estate.text: Gentle trickling sounds all night. Damp, but calming. Do not open the floor hatch. If you do open the floor hatch, close it, and tell nobody.

real_estate.head: Guest Room, Usually Liaison
real_estate.text: Occupied one season a year by a liaison who asks about trade. Available the rest of the year. Do not leave anything behind; it will be discussed as trade.

real_estate.head: Above-the-Workshop Mezzanine
real_estate.text: Close to the forge, the anvil, and every single hammer blow. Ideal for heavy sleepers or dwarves already deafened by previous tenancies. Rent includes ringing.

real_estate.head: Cliffside Nook, First Cavern
real_estate.text: Breathtaking view of glowing fungus trees. Breathtaking neighbours, in that they will take your breath. Fortification wall included. Door strongly recommended.

real_estate.head: Room Inside the Mountain Top
real_estate.text: The highest bedroom in {fort}. Close to the sky, but not too close. Windows sealed for your comfort. Elevation sickness and existential dread included at no charge.

real_estate.head: Flat With Genuine Gem Window
real_estate.text: One wall set with cut stones from our pile of {gems} gems, sparkling in the forge light. Neighbours stare. Thieves stare. Bring curtains, which we don't make.

real_estate.head: Snug Barrel-Cellar Bunk
real_estate.text: Sleep among {drinks} drinks. Guests report waking refreshed, or at least waking. Landlord asks tenants not to tap the walls, or the barrels.

real_estate.head: Migrant Dormitory, Lightly Furnished
real_estate.text: One room, forty beds, one door. Perfect for arrivals who want to meet everyone immediately and very closely. Bring earplugs, a name tag and a sense of humour.

real_estate.head: Lodge on the Pasture Edge
real_estate.text: Stunning view of a herd of {herd}, every one of which also has a stunning view of you. Fresh air, fresh grass, fresh droppings. Not recommended for dwarves who fear the sky or mud.

real_estate.head: Secret Room Behind Bookshelf
real_estate.text: Located somewhere in the library. We're not saying where. Tenants must find it themselves. Three applicants have already failed; one moved into the wrong bookcase.

real_estate.head: Studio Beside the Magma Forge
real_estate.text: Never cold again. Never comfortable again. Laundry dries instantly. So do you. Beard trimming optional, as it trims itself.

real_estate.head: Noble's Former Closet
real_estate.text: Was a closet. Then the noble demanded a bigger room, so it became a closet again. Gilded doorknob retained. Feel important while sleeping upright.

real_estate.head: Watchtower Bunk, Surface Wall
real_estate.text: See goblins coming. See elves coming. See weather coming. You will be the first to know everything and the first to be shot at. Bracing views.

real_estate.head: Cellar With Natural Irrigation
real_estate.text: Excellent for growing fungus, bad for keeping socks dry. Rain on the surface reaches you eventually, as a gentle drip, as a friendly reminder.

announcements.text: A baby boy was born in the tavern this week, between a barrel and a bard. He has been named after the barrel. The bard has written a song about it, which the parents are pretending to enjoy.
A girl was born during the goblin siege. The goblins, hearing the news, paused to send a congratulatory spear. The family has hung it on the nursery wall, point safely outward.
A traveling merchant gave birth at the depot and has asked whether the baby may be counted as trade goods. The broker has declined, firmly but politely.
Congratulations to the youngest dwarf in {fort}, who took her first steps this week directly towards the lever room. She has been gently relocated. Twice.
Triplets were born this week, all with beards. The midwife confirms this is unusual. The father confirms it is normal in his family. The mother has questions.
Two blacksmiths married at the forge, exchanging rings they made themselves in the heat of the ceremony. The rings were too hot to wear. They will wear them next week.
{citizen} and {citizen2} were married on the edge of the first cavern. A giant cave toad attended and was not invited. It ate the cake. The vows were renewed elsewhere.
Two haulers married this week, after meeting while carrying the same stone in opposite directions. They have now agreed on a direction. The stone has been placed on display.
The sheriff married the dwarf he jailed last season. The wedding took place in the jail. The groom insists it was a romantic choice. The bride insists it was convenient.
Our new broker began his tenure by appraising every object in the fort, including his own coat. The coat is worth eight urists. He has started wearing it more confidently.
The fort's new tavern keeper has been installed. His first act was to serve himself. His second was to serve himself again. Business hours are expected to resume shortly.
{promoted} has been elevated to {post}, with full rights to a larger chair. The chair is being built now. Until then, {promoted} is sitting in two regular chairs, side by side.
We have a chief medical dwarf at last. She has already ordered splints, crutches, buckets and, mysteriously, one cat. Asked about the cat, she said 'for morale'.
A visiting scholar has arrived to research 'the effects of beards on intelligence'. He has no beard. He has already been laughed out of the tavern twice.
A monster slayer arrived at the gate and asked for residency. We showed him the caverns. He asked for a different residency. Talks continue.
The latest migrants have arrived with a goat, a cart and a strong opinion about our beds. Please welcome them, and please do not let them redesign the bedrooms.
The caravan arrived with a merchant who sings every price. The broker has asked him to stop. He sang 'no'. Haggling has been described as operatic.
Please welcome {artifact}, the newest resident of {fort}. This fine {artifact_item} emerged with {moodname} after a long, loud week. It will be receiving visitors at its pedestal.
The first mug ever made at {fort} turns one year old. It has been thrown nineteen times, mended twice, and is still the most popular mug in the tavern.
It has been a year since the great wall was finished. The wall has kept out goblins, elves and one stubborn caravan. Celebrations planned at the wall, from the inside.
Happy anniversary to the overseer, who has worked tirelessly for one year by sitting at his desk thinking about the fort. He reports good progress. The fort reports moderate confusion.
One year since {masterwright} finished {masterwork}, and the fort is still talking about it, mainly because {masterwright} brings it up at every meal.
Two miners are engaged after a proposal delivered by striking a vein of gold in the shape of a heart. Experts say it was a coincidence. The couple says it was fate.
{citizen_first} has announced an engagement to a dwarf who has a cat. Friends say the true romance is between {citizen_first} and the cat. The cat has not made a statement.
A mechanic proposed by building a lever that, when pulled, lowers a sign reading 'will you?'. She pulled it. The sign fell on her. She said yes, from the hospital.

sports.head: LEVER-PULLING FINAL ENDS IN FLOOD
sports.body: The inaugural lever-pulling championship ended early when the finalist pulled the wrong lever and flooded the stadium. Judges awarded points for technique, deducted points for the water, and adjourned to the tavern on the floor above.

sports.head: UP/DOWN STAIR CLIMB WON BY A DWARF WHO TOOK THE RAMP
sports.body: Organisers of the hundred-level stair climb have disqualified the winner after it emerged he used a ramp for the final forty levels. He has appealed, arguing that a ramp is 'basically a slanted stair'. The appeal will be heard on level one.

sports.head: CAGE-TRAP DASH: TWO FINISHERS, NINE CAGED
sports.body: Eleven runners entered the cage-trap obstacle course. Two crossed the line. The other nine are being released one at a time by a mechanic who is being paid by the hour and is in no hurry at all.

sports.head: MARKSDWARVES WIN MELEE TOURNAMENT
sports.body: In a stunning upset, the fort's marksdwarves have won the melee tournament by hitting everyone with their crossbows. They have still never fired a bolt. Coaches call this 'a style'. Bowyers call it 'a waste of a good stock'.

sports.head: GIANT TOAD RACING DEBUTS IN THE CAVERN
sports.body: The first season of giant cave toad racing got under way with six toads, six jockeys and one finish line. Five toads sat down. One ate its jockey, briefly. The winning toad hopped twice. Attendance was excellent, mostly from a safe distance.

sports.head: SNOWBALL FIGHT SPILLS INTO TANTRUM
sports.body: A friendly snowball fight on the surface turned unfriendly when a snowball contained a rock, and the rock contained a grudge. Final score: snow 1, everyone else undetermined. Medics have asked players to keep their grudges indoors.

sports.head: CAGED GOBLIN ASKS TO JOIN MILITIA TEAM
sports.body: The goblin captured last season has formally requested a place on the militia sparring team. Coaches admit he has 'real talent and a great work ethic'. The overseer has noted that he also has 'a spear-shaped history'. The cage stays shut.

sports.head: PUMP RELAY: OPERATORS STILL WON'T HAND OVER
sports.body: The pump relay was scheduled to last one hour. It is now in its ninth day because neither operator will let go of the handle 'until the job's done'. The job is unclear. Spectators have brought cots.

sports.head: FISHING DERBY WON WITH A TURTLE
sports.body: The annual fishing derby was won by a dwarf who reeled in a pond turtle, sat on it, and refused to get up. Judges ruled the turtle 'technically a catch'. The turtle has refused to comment, slowly.

sports.head: BEARD-LENGTH OPEN: A TANGLED FINISH
sports.body: The beard-length open ended in confusion when the top three finalists' beards became knotted together on the podium. Judges declared a joint win. The winners have been walking everywhere together since. They say it's fine.

sports.head: BLINDFOLD HAULING TRIALS END AT THE MOAT
sports.body: Contestants in the blindfold hauling trials were asked to carry a stone from the quarry to the stockpile without looking. Most reached the moat. The stone made it the whole way, as nobody was carrying it at the end.

sports.head: PARADE DRILL ABANDONED AFTER UNIFORM MIX-UP
sports.body: The squad's parade drill was cancelled when half the soldiers arrived in full steel and the other half in nothing but helmets. The captain called it 'not ideal'. The crowd called it 'the best parade in years'.

sports.head: FRIENDLY AGAINST FORGOTTEN BEAST ENDS IN FORGOTTEN FRIENDLY
sports.body: An exhibition sparring match against the forgotten beast was scheduled by mistake. Nobody remembers who booked it. Nobody remembers most of the match. The beast now holds the cavern's championship belt, wearing it as a necklace.

sports.head: SPEED-ENGRAVING RECORD FALLS TO A DOODLE
sports.body: An engraver set a new speed record by carving 'a dwarf' in eight seconds. Critics say it is 'a line with a beard'. Officials confirmed the record anyway. The old record holder, who carved a whole siege in a day, is taking it badly.

sports.head: DRAWBRIDGE LONG-JUMP POSTPONED INDEFINITELY
sports.body: The drawbridge long-jump has been postponed after organisers realised the event required someone to raise the bridge while athletes were on it. Volunteers to pull the lever were plentiful. Volunteers to jump were not.

sports.head: MUG-DODGING: DEFENDING CHAMPION RETIRES
sports.body: The fort's undefeated mug-dodger has hung up his helmet after nine seasons. In his farewell speech he thanked his reflexes, his mother and every angry dwarf who ever threw a mug. He was then hit by a mug.

sports.head: SAUSAGE SPRINT CANCELLED: NO SAUSAGE
sports.body: This year's sausage sprint, in which runners chase a sausage on a string, has been cancelled for want of sausage. A rock nut on a string was proposed. Athletes have declined to chase it, citing dignity.

sports.head: COMPETITIVE CAT-SITTING: WINNER NEVER STOOD UP
sports.body: In the cat-sitting championship, contestants must remain seated while a cat sleeps on their lap. The winner has now been seated for eleven days. Organisers are delivering food. The cat has no plans to move.

sports.head: DOG AGILITY TRIAL WON BY THE DOG WHO IGNORED IT
sports.body: The agility trial for the fort's {dogs} dogs was won by a hound who lay down at the start and refused every jump. Judges ruled the other dogs had 'overexerted themselves on obstacles'. The winner was given a bone.

sports.head: MIGRANT GAMES: NEWCOMERS WIN 'FINDING A BED'
sports.body: The welcome games for the latest arrivals included events in finding a bed, finding a different bed, and being told the bed is taken. The newcomers swept all three. The old guard has demanded a rematch in 'having a bed'.

sports.head: UNDERGROUND LAKE RELAY: FISH WIN
sports.body: The cavern-lake relay was abandoned after the third leg when a swimmer was overtaken by a cave fish, then a second cave fish, then a sense of terror. The fish were not entered, but finished first. Medals have been sent to the lake.

sports.head: BOOKKEEPER ENDURANCE COUNT GOES LONG
sports.body: The bookkeeper has entered the endurance count, an event in which competitors count every item in the fort without stopping. He is on item forty thousand. He has no competitors. He is still going. He refuses to be timed.

sports.head: HAMMER THROW: HAMMERER DISQUALIFIED FOR CONTEXT
sports.body: The fort's hammerer has been disqualified from the hammer throw after spectators pointed out his technique 'reminded them of work'. He insists the event is about distance. Nobody stood close enough to measure.

sports.head: NOBLE ENTERS WRESTLING, WINS BY MANDATE
sports.body: The baron entered the wrestling tournament and won every bout by issuing a mandate that his opponents lie down. Referees are reviewing the rulebook. The rulebook is being reviewed by the baron, who has added a page.

sports.head: CARAVAN TUG-OF-WAR: THE YAK WINS
sports.body: A tug-of-war between our haulers and the caravan's guards was settled by the caravan's yak, who pulled both teams into the depot. The yak has been offered a hauling contract. The yak's agent, a merchant, is negotiating.

sports.head: SURFACE SUNBATHING EVENT GETS NO ENTRANTS
sports.body: The first ever surface sunbathing contest was held this summer. Nobody entered. One dwarf walked past on the way to the woodpile and was declared the winner by default. He has asked that his name be withheld.

sports.head: HARVEST DASH: FARMERS FLATTEN THE FARMS
sports.body: The autumn harvest dash was intended to celebrate our farms. Competitors trampled most of them. The winner crossed the line with a single plump helmet, which was then also trampled. Next year's event will be held in a corridor.

sports.head: SPRING THAW REGATTA: BARRELS DIDN'T FLOAT
sports.body: The spring regatta saw six barrels launched into the thawing river with a dwarf in each. All six barrels sank. All six dwarves were recovered. The barrels were recovered later, and are being blamed.

sports.head: HIDE-AND-SEEK FINAL: SEEKER STILL LOOKING
sports.body: The hide-and-seek final began three seasons ago and the hider has not yet been found. Rumours suggest he has walled himself into a room by accident. The mason responsible has been asked to look. He says he's 'pretty sure he wasn't in there'.

sports.head: WHITTLING CUP CONTROVERSY: ELVES OBJECT
sports.body: The whittling cup drew a formal complaint from a visiting elf, who described the event as 'a festival of murder'. The winning entry was a small wooden elf, which only made things worse. The trophy is, unhelpfully, wooden.
