obits.text: {deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. Endlessly curious, they once asked what every lever in the fort did and were told. They wrote it all down. The notes are the only reason the drawbridge still works.
{deadname} has {cause}. A gracious {prof}, they were the only dwarf who ever let the liaison finish a sentence. The liaison has sent a card asking whether this affects the trade agreement.
We remember {deadname}, a {prof} whose first engraving was 'a dwarf' and whose last was 'a dwarf, beautifully'. They have {cause}. Their walls will outlive us all, and frankly judge us.
{deadname}, a {prof}, has {cause}. They gave every barrel in the cellar a name and greeted each by name every morning. The barrels are still here. They miss being called Gerda, Fist and Old Grumble.
{deadname} has {cause}. A patient {prof}, they taught the caged goblin to play cards and lost to him every single time. The goblin has asked to attend the funeral. The cage will be wheeled.
The fortress mourns {deadname}, a {prof} and lifelong defender of ramps over stairs. They have {cause}. A ramp will be named in their honour. The stairs have declined to send flowers.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. They operated the same pump for six straight seasons and were thought by many to be part of it. The pump has been turning slower since. Engineers find no mechanical fault.
Farewell to {deadname}, a {prof} who haggled a human merchant down to paying us for his own wagon. They have {cause}. The merchant's caravan sends condolences and requests the wagon back.
{deadname} has {cause}. A loyal {prof} and veteran of the militia's notorious trouserless season, they never once complained about the draught. A pair of trousers will be buried with them, finally.
We say goodbye to {deadname}, a {prof} who knew where every hatch in the fortress led. They have {cause}. Several hatches now lead to places nobody can identify. Please do not open the green one.
{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. They tamed a giant cave toad using only patience and cheese, and rode it, once, the length of the cavern. The toad has been told. It sat down for a long while.

{deadname} has {cause}. A serene {prof}, they never threw a single mug in their entire life, a feat that left their friends deeply suspicious. A mug has been placed on the slab, unthrown, as a tribute.

The fortress has lost {deadname}, a {prof} who engraved more memorial slabs than anyone in our history. They have {cause}. Out of respect, their slab is being engraved by three dwarves at once. It is a little crowded.
{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. They liked to walk across the frozen river every winter, 'to check'. They always reported back that it was frozen. We will check ourselves now, from the bank.

{deadname} has {cause}. A thoughtful {prof}, they claimed four separate bedrooms over their lifetime and slept in none of them, preferring the dining hall floor. The bedrooms have been reassigned. The floor has been left alone.

Farewell to {deadname}, a {prof} survived by one loyal yak who follows nobody else and stands at the tomb door each morning. They have {cause}. The yak has been given a blanket and a small sign reading 'good yak'.

{deadname}, a {prof}, has {cause}. They greeted every migrant wave at the gate personally, with a mug and the words 'the beds are that way, sort of'. The next arrivals will be met by a sign that says the same.

We remember {deadname}, a {prof} who dyed everything they owned a single shade of blue, including, on one occasion, the overseer. They have {cause}. The fort will wear blue this week, some of it permanently.

{deadname} has {cause}. A devoted {prof}, they polished {artifact} every morning, though nobody asked them to and it was already perfect. The artifact looks slightly duller today. Everyone has noticed.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. Over a long life they escaped the hospital nine times, once while still in traction. The chief medical dwarf calls them 'the worst patient I ever loved'. A crutch has been retired in their honour.
Farewell to {deadname}, a {prof} who could tell you, at any moment, exactly how many {stone} stones we had. They have {cause}. Nobody knows the number now. We are told it is 'a lot'.

{deadname} has {cause}. A merry {prof}, they gave everyone in {fort} a nickname, and most of them stuck. Several dwarves are now unsure of their real names. The bookkeeper will sort it out, eventually.

The forge falls silent for {deadname}, a {prof} who hummed in time with the hammer and could keep a tune through a whole steel breastplate. They have {cause}. The smiths will hum their song this week, slightly off-beat.
{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. Friends ask that a slab be engraved within the week, as {deadname} was always punctual and would hate to haunt anyone late. The engravers have been notified, firmly.

We say farewell to {deadname}, a {prof} who mapped the first cavern by walking every inch of it and naming each mushroom tree. They have {cause}. The map is in the library. It is mostly drawings of mushrooms with names.

gossip.text: Whispers in the corridors say {citizen} knows what the unlabelled lever does and is refusing to tell anyone. {citizen} insists there is no unlabelled lever. Nobody has asked which lever.

The caged goblin's card games have become the hottest ticket in the fort. Players report he cheats, gloats and offers excellent conversation. A waiting list has formed. The cage has been moved closer to the tavern.
Overheard at breakfast: nobody has ever seen the bookkeeper eat, sleep or go outside. Friends say he's simply dedicated. Others have begun leaving garlic-shaped rocks near his office, just in case.

Society insiders report that the baron has demanded a throne, received a throne, and then demanded a slightly different throne. The old throne is now in the tavern, where it has become the most fought-over seat in {fort}.
{citizen} has started calling {citizen2} 'Thunderbeard'. {citizen2} has started calling {citizen} 'Drizzlechin'. Both claim to be winning. Neighbours have chosen sides and nicknames of their own.

Two miners have been spending a suspicious amount of time 'surveying' the first cavern together. Witnesses report they have surveyed the same mushroom tree eleven times. The toads are said to be supportive.

A quarrel over who gets the good chair in the tavern ended with both dwarves sitting in it at once. They have now spent three evenings in silence, side by side, neither willing to concede. It's being called a romance by some.

{citizen} was dismayed to discover an engraving of themselves on the dining hall wall, looking 'unflatteringly surprised'. The engraver says it was drawn from life. {citizen} says they were only surprised because of the engraver.

The fortress rumour mill is turning on the question of the dwarf who never touches wine. Sources say it is a vampire. Other sources say it is a dwarf with a strict brewer's diet. The dwarf, asked, just smiled. Too widely.

The kitchen has been losing one wheel of cheese a night. Insiders say the chef has begun sleeping in the larder. Witnesses say the chef has been seen in the larder, eating cheese, asleep. The investigation continues.

Two dwarves with pet yaks are not speaking after one yak ate the other's hat. The owners met to settle the matter, and both yaks ate both hats. The owners now share a common grievance and are, apparently, friends.

Hospital staff report a blossoming romance between a patient and the dwarf who keeps bringing water. Friends say the patient has been 'mysteriously re-injured' four times this season. The water-bringer says it's 'just good service'.

The fort's dyers are at war after one of them dyed the other's beard blue while he slept. The victim has responded by dyeing his rival's entire bedroom. Interior decorators call it 'the bluest feud in history'.

{citizen_first} has lost a nickname. The old nickname, 'Hammerfist', was abandoned after an incident at the bakery. Several new nicknames have been proposed. {citizen_first} has rejected all of them, especially 'Breadfist'.

One of the new arrivals is said to have been famous back home, for something involving a cart and a hill. The details are unclear, but the fort's welcome has been noticeably warmer, mostly in hopes of hearing the story.

The caravan's guard captain was seen sharing a mug with {citizen} on the depot steps. The caravan has now left. {citizen} has been on the depot steps every evening since, staring at the road, with two mugs.
{promoted} has thrown three parties in a week to celebrate becoming {post}. Guests report the parties are nice, if a little heavy on speeches about how hard it is to be {post}.
Since emerging with {artifact}, {moodname} has been seen visiting it daily and whispering to it. Close friends say this is normal after a mood. Other friends say it is normal for {moodname} anyway.

Since {masterwright} made {masterwork}, several rival craftsdwarves have been working late. One has produced a masterwork of their own: a mug reading 'not bad, {masterwright}'. It is very finely made.

A dwarf tried to propose at the top of the up/down staircase this week, but by the time the partner climbed up to hear it, both were too winded to speak. They settled for a nod. Friends say it counts.
Gossips have been asking why a door near the cellar has been forbidden since spring. The overseer says it's 'nothing'. The mechanic says it's 'something'. The noise behind it says it's 'hungry'.

The kennel master is said to be devastated after a dog he raised from a puppy decided it preferred the butcher. Insiders say it was 'just a matter of smell'. The kennel master has started carrying sausages in his pocket.

Rumour has it {citizen} and {citizen2} are planning a wedding, but cannot agree on a venue: one wants the forge, the other wants the library. A compromise has been reached: the corridor between them, which is long, draughty and neutral.

Two bards are in an escalating feud over who sings louder. The first performed on the stairs. The second performed on the surface. The first is now planning a concert in the magma forge, which everyone hopes is a bluff.

Several readers have written in about a rumoured secret room behind the library's bookshelves. The librarian says there is no secret room. The librarian was later seen walking into a bookshelf and not coming out.

Fashion watchers report that dwarves short of pairs are now wearing odd socks as scarves. The trend started with {citizen}, who had one sock and a cold neck, and has since spread wildly through the fort.

The overseer has taken up whittling, which has made the elves furious and the woodworkers nervous. His first carving is a small wooden overseer. Several dwarves say it does more work than the original.
A human merchant is said to have written a love letter to our depot. Not a dwarf at the depot. The depot itself. He described its ramps as 'majestic'. The broker has filed the letter under 'trade'.

The fort's two cooks have been preparing increasingly elaborate meals to impress the noble. The noble has eaten every one and said 'adequate' to each. Both cooks are now plotting against the noble, together.
Sources report that someone has been hiding snowballs in the cellar to throw at unsuspecting dwarves later in the year. The prank has so far failed, as the snowballs have all become small puddles.

A dwarf who spent an hour on the surface this summer has returned with a sunburned nose and an air of great importance. He has told everyone. He has shown everyone. Some have asked him to stop pointing at it.

{citizen} spent an afternoon staring at a pile of bones and muttering, which caused a panic about a strange mood. It turned out {citizen} was just trying to remember where they left their pick. The pick was in the bones.

Several dwarves are said to be in love with {artifact}. The {artifact_item} has received anonymous gifts, flowers and one poem. Its maker finds this flattering, then concerning, then deeply concerning.

The latest ghost in the corridors is said to have strong opinions about the new bedroom layout. It has been seen rearranging chairs at night. Several dwarves have admitted the new layout is better and the ghost is right.
Two dwarves are locked in a custody battle over a kitten that adopted both of them on the same afternoon. The sheriff has proposed shared custody. The kitten has proposed a third dwarf entirely.

weather_jokes.text: Rain falling on the surface. Down here we have a roof made of a whole mountain, which is the correct amount of roof.
A rainy day for the elves, who will spend it standing in the downpour thanking the trees for drinking. We will spend it indoors, drinking for the trees.
Rain on the surface is good news for any surface farms, and bad news for anyone carrying cloth to the depot. Pick one and live with it.
Light rain on the pasture. The herd will be wet, the herd will smell, and the herd will want to come inside. Do not let the herd come inside.
Rain expected. Any caravan on the road will be late, damp and in no mood to haggle, which is the ideal time to haggle.
Snow on the surface, which helpfully shows the footprints of everything walking around up there. We advise not studying them too closely.
Fresh snow today. Beards worn outdoors may collect it. Beards collecting more than a handful will be considered wildlife and treated accordingly.
Snowy conditions mean the elves can no longer pretend it's always spring in their forest. We expect a strongly worded letter blaming us.
Snow lying deep on the surface. Miners say it's 'just soft stone'. Do not mine the snow. Do not smooth the snow. Do not engrave the snow.
Snow and frost expected, which slows goblins down. It slows dwarves down more. On balance, an excellent day to stay behind the drawbridge.
Clear skies today with strong sunlight. Dwarves on surface duty should squint heroically and pretend it is the glow of a forge.
A clear day, which brings out the birds. Keep an eye on your bracelets, rings and crowns. The birds have been watching your jewellery for some time.
Fine and dry today. Excellent woodcutting weather, say the woodcutters. Terrible woodcutting weather, say the trees, through their elven spokesmen.
Clear skies tonight, ideal for stargazing. Anyone wishing to look at the stars may do so through the narrow slot in the fortification, one eye at a time.
A warm front is spreading from the forges towards the dining hall, bringing smoky conditions and scattered sparks. Beards should be tucked in.
Thick fog in the first cavern this morning, created by something breathing heavily. We hope it is the moss. We suspect it is not the moss.
Light mist expected near the waterfall, as usual. Dwarves passing through will feel refreshed and slightly happier. Dwarves who stop to enjoy it will be hauled away by a busy colleague.
A stiff draught is blowing through the east corridor since someone left the surface door open. The door has been closed. The draught has been blamed on a ghost anyway.
Drought warning: barrels in the tavern have fallen to {drinks}. Conditions are expected to become dry, then tense, then throwy.
Flood warning in the cellar: {drinks} drinks on hand and rising. Dwarves are advised to drink responsibly, then drink a little more, to ease pressure on the barrels.
Spring has arrived on the surface, bringing mud, more mud and a swarm of very small flies. Every dwarf who went outside this week has come back covered in at least two of these.
A hot summer day on the surface. The pond is warm, the grass is crisp, and the elves are lying on rocks like lizards. A good day to stay below and pretend none of this is happening.
Autumn winds are picking up, blowing leaves into the depot and into the soup. Cooks say the leaves 'add texture'. Diners say they add leaves.
Winter is here and the surface has gone quiet, except for the wind, the wolves and the distant sound of an elf apologising to a frozen tree.
Outside today: {weather}. Inside today: forge-warm, rock-solid, and a light shower of mugs near the tavern by evening.
Tantrum warning in effect for the craftsdwarf corridor after a mandate was ignored. Expect scattered shouting and isolated furniture breakage. Shelter behind a bench.
Magma level slightly higher this week. Humidity remains very low, temperature remains very high, and the forge crew remains extremely cheerful about it.
The miasma front over the butcher's shop has cleared. Visibility is good, smells are fine, and the refuse pile has been moved further away, for now.
Persistent drizzle continues on level six, as the aquifer has decided to come and visit. Bring a bucket. Bring an umbrella. Bring a mason with spare blocks.
It is {season} in year {year}. The surface is doing whatever it does in {season}. The fort is doing what it always does, which is drinking and digging.

corrections.text: Last issue we said the lever by the dining hall 'opens the pantry'. It does not. It opens the floodgate. We apologise to everyone in the dining hall, and to the pantry, which remains closed.
We previously referred to the caged goblin as 'Kevin'. He has asked us to point out that his name is Snodub Gorespear. He has also asked that we keep calling him Kevin, as he has grown fond of it.
Our report said the liaison had 'no further questions'. This was optimistic. He has many further questions. All of them are about trade.
An announcement last week said the giant cave toad was best man at a wedding. It was a guest. It did not perform any duties. It ate the cake, which is not a duty.
We described the drawbridge as 'a safe place to stand'. It is a safe place to stand only when it is down. We regret the error, and so does the dwarf who now lives on the far side of the moat.
A map printed last issue showed a staircase where there is in fact a ramp. Readers who attempted to climb the ramp as stairs are reminded that ramps are also climbable, just differently.
We reported that the bookkeeper is a vampire. We have been asked to state that the bookkeeper is not a vampire, and to state it after sundown, when the bookkeeper can read it personally.
Last issue claimed the new windmill 'runs on enthusiasm'. It runs on wind. On calm days it does not run at all, regardless of how enthusiastically the millers shout at it.
We stated that {artifact} was worth 'quite a bit'. The correct value is 'more than this entire newspaper office, the staff and our cat'. We apologise to the artifact.
Last issue listed the forbidden door near the cellar as 'probably fine'. Please disregard. Please do not open the door. Please do not lean on the door. Please stop knocking on the door.
We said a dwarf was 'taken by a fey mood'. The dwarf in question was taken by a nap. They have since woken up and produced nothing at all, which we apologise for suggesting otherwise.
A previous issue said the overseer's beard was dyed blue 'as a fashion statement'. The overseer was asleep at the time. The statement was made by the dyer. We regret the confusion.

We previously described the latest migrant wave as 'small'. It was not small. Our reporter counted the first cart and then went to lunch. {pop} dwarves now live here. Several of them are in our office.
Last issue congratulated the wrong dwarf on becoming {post}. The correct dwarf is {promoted}. The wrong dwarf has enjoyed the attention very much and has asked if he can keep the hat.
In our last issue, {masterwork} was credited to 'some dwarf'. It was made by {masterwright}, who has contacted us several times to make sure we know. We know.
We reported that miners had struck 'something shiny'. It was {mineral}. Our science desk would like to stress that 'shiny' is not a mineral, and has been sent back to the library.
Our caravan report listed 'three bins of rare cheese'. Two of the bins were cheese. The third bin was the merchant, napping. He has asked for a mention, and an apology for the word 'rare'.
Our recent notice about {deadname} contained an embarrassing error about the cause of death. We apologise to the family, the hospital, and to the carp, who was not involved this time.
We reported last issue that the tavern had 'plenty' of drink. The bookkeeper says the figure is {drinks}. Readers are asked to adjust their expectations and their pace.
We reported a 'meat sighting' near the kitchen. It was a mushroom shaped like a sausage. Dwarves who rushed to the kitchen are asked to return to work and to put the mushroom down.
Last week's forecast called for 'sand'. We meant snow. Dwarves who went outside expecting a pleasant beach day are thawing in the hospital and do not want to hear from us.

We used the nickname 'Drizzlechin' for {citizen}. This nickname is not used by anyone except {citizen2}. We apologise to {citizen}, who has asked to be called 'Thunderbeard', which nobody uses either.
A caption last issue read 'An engraving of a dwarf and a cheese. The dwarf is laughing.' In fact, the cheese is laughing. The dwarf is weeping. We regret misreading the room.
We said the baron's new throne was 'grand'. The baron has asked us to amend this to 'very grand'. The carpenter has asked us to amend it to 'two chairs nailed together'. We print both.
We reported that the hospital had 'no shortage of crutches'. The hospital has three crutches and twelve patients. The shortage is real, and so is the queue for the good crutch.
Our previous issue dismissed bogeymen as a myth. Following a large number of letters, all written in shaky handwriting and many received at night, we now accept bogeymen are real. Stay indoors.
We previously claimed the fortress 'smells fine'. Our reporter had a cold. Since recovering, he has withdrawn the claim, and the article, and has been seen running towards the soapmaker's workshop.
We said the kitchen lost a cheese 'to a thief'. The chef has since confessed he ate it while sleepwalking. The thief, a goblin, has asked us to clear his name of this one specifically.
We wrote that the weather was {weather} across the whole of {world}. This was an overreach. Our weather desk only looked out of one door.
Our masthead last week claimed it was 'about year something'. It is year {year}. The editor responsible has been given a calendar and strong encouragement to look at it.
We misidentified the god worshipped in our temple as 'the god of rivers and boredom'. The correct title is 'the god of rivers and patience'. Worshippers were too patient to complain until now.
We reported the well as 'ten levels deep'. It is ten levels deep, then a lake, then a cave, then something that hums. Please do not drop more buckets in to check.
We congratulated the masons on 'freshly engraved' walls. The walls were only smoothed. The engraving is next year. The masons enjoyed the praise and have asked if they can keep it.
Our Funny Pages credited last week's comic to the fortress's bard. It was drawn by a child. The child is offended. The bard is relieved. The comic was better than the bard's.
Last issue's safety notice said 'beware the weapon traps' when it should have said 'beware the weapon traps, and the cage traps, and the stone-fall traps, and just generally the gate'.
We reported the fort has {dogs} dogs. One of them has written to say he is 'more of a wolf'. We have checked. He is a dog. We decline to correct the figure.
The obituaries column last issue was written about a dwarf who turned out to be an alive yak. The yak is fine. We regret the error, and the yak regrets the flowers.
Our recipe page advised 'searing your steak over the magma channel'. Do not do this. The steak will not survive. Nor will the spatula. Nor, in one tragic test case, the chef's eyebrows.
An earlier story described the visiting elves as 'twice as tall as a dwarf'. They are roughly one and a half times as tall. They also asked us to note that they are 'twice as wise'. We have declined.
We reported that the library holds 'many books'. It holds four books, two of which are about rocks. One of the other two is a menu. The librarian asks you to come and read it.

world_news.head: LIAISON LOST BETWEEN {hillock} AND {fort}
world_news.body: The mountainhome's outpost liaison set out for {hillock} two seasons ago and has not been seen since. Search parties report finding a trail of abandoned questionnaires about trade. Each one is unanswered. Each one is signed hopefully.

world_news.head: {darkfort} OPENS LIBRARY; ALL BOOKS ABOUT SPEARS
world_news.body: The goblins of {darkfort} have opened their first public library. It contains four hundred books, every one titled 'Spear'. Scholars from {town} visited and report the prose is 'repetitive but sincere'. Late fees are paid in prisoners.

world_news.head: ELF CAUGHT WITH WOODEN SPOON AT {retreat}
world_news.body: An elf at {retreat} has been publicly shamed after a wooden spoon was found in his hut. He insists the spoon 'grew that way'. The spoon has been given a state funeral. The elf has been sentenced to eating soup with his hands.

world_news.head: {town} AND {town2} AT ODDS OVER CHEESE
world_news.body: Trade between {town} and {town2} has collapsed after a dispute about which city's cheese is 'more yellow'. Both cities have now banned the other's cheese. Smugglers report record profits and a strong yellow smell along the border.

world_news.head: KOBOLDS SEND AMBASSADOR; HE STEALS EMBASSY
world_news.body: The kobolds of {world} have sent their first ambassador to {town2}. He presented his credentials, made a stirring speech, and was found that night carrying the embassy's front door down the road. Talks are said to be continuing, without a door.

world_news.head: TITAN SPOTTED NEAR {hillock}, ASKS FOR DIRECTIONS
world_news.body: Travellers near {hillock} report a titan of great size stopped them on the road to ask the way to the nearest dwarven fortress. They pointed in the opposite direction. Our correspondent wishes to thank them personally.

world_news.head: NECROMANCER DRAWS PENSIONS FOR ENTIRE ARMY
world_news.body: Officials at {town} have discovered that a local necromancer has been claiming retirement pensions for four hundred undead soldiers. He argues they are 'technically veterans'. A hearing has been scheduled, which the soldiers will attend in silence.

world_news.head: {hillock} BREWERS STRIKE OVER BARREL SIZES
world_news.body: Brewers at {hillock} have laid down their mugs in protest at a new noble mandate requiring 'smaller, more elegant barrels'. Production has stopped. Tantrums have started. The noble has been offered a very small, very elegant barrel, at speed.

world_news.head: {darkfort2} ANNOUNCES 'SIEGE-FREE SEASON'
world_news.body: In a surprise move, {darkfort2} has declared a season without sieges so its soldiers can 'rest, reflect and sharpen things'. Neighbouring fortresses have welcomed the news and are using the time to sharpen things of their own.

world_news.head: {town2} INTRODUCES TAX ON LOOKING AT THE SKY
world_news.body: The humans of {town2} have introduced a tax on any citizen caught looking upward. Dwarven visitors have been delighted to discover they owe nothing. Humans are said to be walking around staring firmly at their feet.

world_news.head: {retreat} REJECTS STONE STATUE AS 'TOO STILL'
world_news.body: A statue gifted to {retreat} as a gesture of friendship has been returned with a note complaining that it 'doesn't grow, doesn't sway, and doesn't do anything at all'. The sculptor has replied that this was the whole point.

world_news.head: CARAVAN FROM {town} DELIVERS TO WRONG FORTRESS
world_news.body: A human caravan bound for us arrived instead at {hillock}, which accepted all the goods, thanked the merchants, and sent them home. The merchants have only just noticed. {hillock} has sent a thank-you note.

world_news.head: MAPMAKERS ADD A MOUNTAIN TO {world} BY ACCIDENT
world_news.body: A mountain drawn on the latest maps of {world} has been revealed to be a dribble of dwarven ale. Explorers sent to climb it found a flat field and an awkward silence. The stain is still listed as the highest point in the region.

world_news.head: FORGOTTEN BEAST NEAR {town} 'JUST WANTS TO BE REMEMBERED'
world_news.body: A forgotten beast in the caverns under {town} has reportedly asked visitors to tell people about it. 'It's in the name,' said one witness. 'It's lonely.' The beast is said to have eaten the witness's companion while making this point.

world_news.head: GOBLIN COOKBOOK BECOMES SURPRISE BESTSELLER
world_news.body: 'Feasts of {darkfort}' has become the season's most popular book among humans of {town2}, mostly as a horror novel. The author is said to be delighted, confused, and preparing a second volume entitled 'More Meat'.

world_news.head: {hillock} MAYOR'S HAT DECLARED A SEPARATE NOBLE
world_news.body: After years of being consulted on matters of state, the mayor of {hillock}'s hat has been formally granted its own title. It is now Baroness of Brims. Its first mandate demands a smaller dwarf beneath it.

world_news.head: HUMAN KNIGHT VOWS TO SLAY DRAGON, SLAYS LIZARD
world_news.body: A knight from {town} who swore to slay the dragon of {world} has returned triumphant, carrying the body of a medium-sized lizard. Asked about the discrepancy, he pointed out that the lizard 'had a very bad attitude'.

world_news.head: {retreat} HOLDS ELECTION; TREE WINS
world_news.body: The elves of {retreat} have elected an ancient oak as their new leader, after it received every vote cast. Opposition elves argue the tree did not campaign. Supporters say that is exactly why it won.

world_news.head: {darkfort} FORGETS WHO IT IS AT WAR WITH
world_news.body: Goblin generals at {darkfort} have admitted they no longer remember who they are fighting. 'We have the spears,' said one, 'and the enthusiasm. We're just missing a target.' Every neighbouring settlement has been asked to keep very quiet.

world_news.head: {town} SCHOLARS CONFIRM BATHING 'NOT DANGEROUS'
world_news.body: A study by the scholars of {town} has concluded that regular bathing does not weaken the body or anger the gods. Dwarven readers are urged to treat these findings with the caution due to any study done above ground.

world_news.head: {hillock} ASKS TO BORROW OUR ARTIFACT
world_news.body: Officials at {hillock} have written to request a loan of {artifact} for their great hall, 'just for a season'. Our overseer has replied that the last thing we lent {hillock} was a bucket, which is still being discussed.

world_news.head: IT RAINED UP IN {town2}, WITNESSES SAY
world_news.body: Residents of {town2} report a brief period of rain falling upward last week. Scholars blame 'weather'. Dwarven experts blame 'the sky, generally'. Nobody blames the necromancer, who was seen nearby, giggling.

world_news.head: NEW ROAD LINKS {town} TO {darkfort}; NOBODY USES IT
world_news.body: A paved road now connects the human city of {town} with the goblin stronghold at {darkfort}. Traffic has been light, consisting of one merchant who misread the signs and a large number of goblins heading in only one direction.

world_news.head: SCHOLARS OF {world} SPLIT OVER 'IS A ROCK A STONE'
world_news.body: A conference of the great minds of {world} broke up in disarray after two days of debating whether rocks and stones are the same thing. A dwarven delegate who said 'obviously yes' was escorted out for 'oversimplifying'.

world_news.head: {hillock} REPORTS MIGRANTS MOVING TO {fort}
world_news.body: Leaders at {hillock} have complained that their dwarves keep leaving for {fort}, citing 'better barrels and a more interesting newspaper'. We are flattered. We have also run out of beds. Please slow down.

world_news.head: SNATCHERS OF {darkfort2} FORM A UNION
world_news.body: Goblin snatchers at {darkfort2} have unionised, demanding shorter nights, longer sacks and a bonus for every baby returned in good condition. Their employers are said to be furious. Their victims are said to be quietly supportive.

world_news.head: {town} NEIGHBOURS COMPLAIN OF TOWER NOISE
world_news.body: Residents near the necromancer's tower outside {town} have filed complaints about late-night rattling, moaning and organ music. The necromancer has apologised for the organ music and refused to apologise for anything else.

world_news.head: ELF AND DWARF FRIENDS FOR THIRTY YEARS, BOTH EMBARRASSED
world_news.body: A dwarf from {hillock} and an elf from {retreat} have revealed a decades-long friendship. 'We don't talk about trees,' the elf explained. 'We don't talk about chairs,' said the dwarf. 'We mostly don't talk.' Both families are appalled.

world_news.head: DRAGON'S LAIR NEAR {town2} UNDERGOES RENOVATION
world_news.body: The famous dragon's lair outside {town2} has been remodelled after the dragon complained about 'drafts and adventurers'. New features include a front door, a back door and a sign reading 'NO HEROES'. Heroes say the sign is 'a challenge'.

world_news.head: HISTORIANS SAY {world} IS 'ROUGHLY OLD'
world_news.body: After decades of research, historians have announced that the world of {world} is 'quite old, roughly'. They have not been more specific. Asked how old exactly, the head historian said 'older than me', then sat down for a long rest.

travel.head: {darkfort2}: BED AND BREAKFAST, MOSTLY BREAKFAST
travel.body: The goblins of {darkfort2} are proud of their new guesthouse. There is no bed. Breakfast is served at all hours, sometimes by surprise, sometimes to you. Our reviewer left with a full stomach and a profound suspicion about what it was full of.

travel.head: {hillock} LIBRARY TOUR
travel.body: {hillock} boasts the largest dwarven library in the region, all six books of it. Our guide read us the first chapter of each, then asked us to leave because we had read too much. The gift shop sells the same six books, slightly cheaper.

travel.head: {town} FISH MARKET: LOUD
travel.body: Humans at the {town} fish market shout prices at each other from a distance of three feet. Nobody seems to buy anything. Everyone seems happy. Our reporter bought a fish, was shouted at for buying the fish, and fled with the fish. Lovely fish.

travel.head: STAYING IN A TREE AT {retreat}
travel.body: Our hosts at {retreat} offered us a room inside a living tree. It creaked all night, swayed in the wind, and dropped an acorn on our reviewer every hour, on the hour. The elves say the tree 'liked us'. We left before it liked us more.

travel.head: THE GREAT MOUNTAINS OF {world}: A PROPER HOLIDAY
travel.body: At last, a destination worthy of a dwarf: vast mountains, stone everywhere, and no trees above a certain point. We spent three blissful days staring at granite. Our only regret is that we had to come back down, where the sky is.

travel.head: {darkfort}'S FAMOUS MOAT OF SPIKES
travel.body: The tour guide at {darkfort} spent half an hour explaining the moat of spikes, its history, its many victims and its 'rich cultural meaning'. We asked if we could go round it. He laughed for twenty minutes. We went round it. It took a week.

travel.head: AN EVENING AT THE {town2} OPERA
travel.body: The human opera at {town2} lasted five hours and was about a man who could not decide whether to marry. In the end he married. Nobody was crushed, burnt or eaten. The audience called it 'heartbreaking'. We were baffled and also bored.

travel.head: {hillock} MUD BATHS: ACCIDENTALLY RELAXING
travel.body: The mud baths at {hillock} are, we discovered, the result of a burst aquifer that nobody fixed. Locals have made the best of it. Our reviewer sat in the mud for an hour and emerged calmer, dirtier, and unable to locate one of his boots.

travel.head: BY CARAVAN TO {darkfort}: DON'T
travel.body: We joined a merchant caravan heading for {darkfort}, under the impression it was a trade mission. It was a trade mission. We were the goods. Our reviewer was eventually returned, having been judged 'too complain-y' for resale.

travel.head: {retreat} SPRING FESTIVAL
travel.body: The elves of {retreat} celebrate spring with a festival of dancing among flowers. Our reviewer was asked to join and did, stiffly, in boots. A circle formed around him. It was not admiration. It was the elves, keeping their distance from the boots.

travel.head: THE DUNGEONS OF {town} CASTLE
travel.body: We were delighted to find something underground in {town}, and toured the castle dungeons with real enthusiasm. Damp, dark, beautifully cut stone. Our reviewer asked to stay a night. The guards agreed, and only let him out after a week.

travel.head: THE COAST OF {world}: A LOT OF WATER
travel.body: We travelled to the coast to see the sea. It is a large amount of water with no walls. The carp there are bigger, angrier and many. Our reviewer did not go in, did not get near, and has asked us never to send him anywhere wet again.

travel.head: A TAVERN CRAWL OF {hillock}
travel.body: {hillock} has only one tavern, but its corridors are so long that walking from one end of the bar to the other counts as a crawl. Fine drink, friendly locals, and a shocking lack of chairs. We drank standing. It felt like home.

travel.head: {darkfort2} ARENA: FRONT-ROW SEATS
travel.body: The fighting pits of {darkfort2} offer front-row seats to every visitor. Unfortunately, the front row is in the pit. Our reviewer won two bouts, lost one, and returned home with a trophy, a limp and a contract he did not sign.

travel.head: WALKING THE {town2} BRIDGE
travel.body: The humans of {town2} are very proud of their great stone bridge, a fine structure crossing a river full of carp. Our reviewer walked it in eleven seconds, very fast, without looking down. He gives it five stars, from a distance.

travel.head: ELVEN TEA AT {retreat}
travel.body: The elves served tea made from leaves, flowers, a small twig and one moth. They called it 'the forest in a cup'. It tasted like a forest, specifically the floor of it. Our reviewer drank it to be polite and has been unwell since.

travel.head: {town} SKY FESTIVAL: ALARMING
travel.body: The humans of {town} hold an annual festival to celebrate 'the open sky'. It consists of standing in a field, looking up. Our reviewer attended under a large hat and a small table. He survived. He does not recommend it.

travel.head: THE DESERTS OF {world}: SAND
travel.body: We visited the great desert to the south. It is all sand. No stone, no water, no shade and no barrels. A camel tried to eat our map. We let it. The map was also mostly sand by then. Zero stars, which is also how many trees there were.

travel.head: {hillock} FORGE TOUR: WARM WELCOME
travel.body: The forges of {hillock} glow day and night, and visitors are welcome to watch the smiths at work, which they do very loudly. Our reviewer received a small iron souvenir and a large scorch mark. He has framed both.

travel.head: THE GIFT SHOP AT {darkfort}
travel.body: We are told the tower of {darkfort} now has a gift shop. It sells spears, little spears, spear keyrings, and postcards of spears. We bought a mug. It was also a spear. The mug cannot hold drink, but we use it as a spear.

letters_abroad.body: The beds in {town} are so high off the ground that I need a ladder to get into one. I asked the humans why they sleep so far up. They asked me why I sleep 'in a hole'. Neither of us won. I sleep on the floor now. It is the only correct height.

The elves at {retreat} have named a tree after me, as a gesture of goodwill. It is a very small tree. I have checked the others, and they are all named after elves and much larger. I suspect a message. Please advise.

Your newspaper arrived at {darkfort} at last. The goblins read it aloud and laughed at all the wrong parts, especially the obituaries. They've asked for a subscription. I've told them it'll cost them my freedom. They are thinking about it.

A dwarf at {hillock} went into a fey mood and demanded our fortress's artifact as raw material. I am writing to ask whether you would lend it. It would only be for a moment. She would only sort of destroy it.
I've made a human friend in {town2}. He is very tall and asks lots of questions about beards. I've answered them all. He has started growing one. It is thin and sad. Please send advice. And a comb.
letters_abroad.by: A Dwarf of Good Cheer, in {town2}

letters_abroad.body: I have now walked across the whole of {world} and wish to report that it is, in my estimate, mostly grass. I came home to tell you this in person, but nobody would listen at the gate, so I am writing to the paper.

Since my capture at {darkfort2}, I have been put to work in the goblin kitchens. They have no concept of cheese. I have introduced it. There is now a small cheese cult forming among the guards. I am not sure I will be released, or that I want to be.

I write to complain that {fort} has been sending us its migrants' worst habits. They arrived at {hillock}, slept in our dining hall, sang until morning and stole our good mugs. We would like them back. The habits, not the dwarves.

The guards of {town} keep stopping me to ask if I'm a child. I am a hundred and four. I have a beard to my belt. I have explained this. They have apologised and then asked whether my parents know where I am. Please help.

The elves of {retreat} invited me to a feast, which was a bowl of berries and a long speech about the berries. I asked whether there would be a second course. The elves said 'this is the second course'. I am writing from hunger.

I have escaped from {darkfort} and wish to thank the goblin guard who left the gate open. He did it on purpose. He wished me well. He asked me to tell everyone he is 'not like the other goblins'. I've told you. Please don't tell the other goblins.

It has been raining in {town2} for nineteen days. The humans carry small cloth roofs on sticks. I have asked to borrow one and been told 'everybody has their own'. I am building one of stone. It is heavy. Progress is slow.

Please inform the beard-length contest at {fort} that {hillock} wishes to challenge. Our champion's beard is long enough to tie in a knot around a cart, which she has done. The cart is ours. We will bring it.

I purchased a map of {world} from your advertisers and followed it faithfully. It led me into a lake. I am writing from the lake. The map is also in the lake. I would like a refund, preferably a dry one.

The humans of {town} have a fine market, good bread and pleasant manners. They do not have ceilings outdoors. I have asked about this repeatedly. They tell me it's 'the sky'. I think they are making excuses.

Would whoever left an axe outside the gates of {retreat} please collect it? The elves have been weeping at it daily for a month. They have built a little fence around it. It is now a shrine to the dangers of dwarves. I would like my axe back.

I am a goblin of {darkfort2} and I have read your paper for a year. I want to say that I like the comics. I do not like the obituaries, as several are about my cousins. Please print more comics. And fewer cousins.

Our noble at {hillock} wishes to trade a dozen steel goblets for a single barrel of your famous ale. Our noble has never tasted your ale. He just likes the idea of being envied. Please send it and say nothing.

I have been invited to a human wedding in {town2} and asked to bring a gift. I have carved them a fine granite bowl. They asked why it is so heavy. I asked why their table is made of wood. The wedding is now on hold.

I am the oldest dwarf I know in {world}, and the secret to a long life is simple: drink at every meal, never go outside, and never, under any circumstances, ask a lever what it does. Please print this. My grandchildren don't listen.

lines: BRING A ROOF THAT FOLLOWS YOU
Four dwarves, one slab, one sense of security. Bearers paid by the hour. Bearers may tire. Roof may fall.
Key phrases: 'please', 'no thank you', 'that is my leg'. Audio course is mostly screaming. Course completed by 3 dwarves.
Fools most elves for up to six minutes. Do not speak. Do not sit on any furniture. Do not reveal the axe.
All trades final. Dwarves returned only with matching socks. We will not take back bards.
Covers bites, nibbles and full swallowings. Claims assessed by our panel of carp. Panel has never paid out.
Six hundred pages of caves, cellars and tunnels. Surface sections left blank for your own safety.
Skeletons polished, zombies freshened, necromancers politely ignored. Not liable for anything that gets up again.
Thick smoky lenses for dwarves abroad. Blocks glare, sky and most of your surroundings. Do not wear near rivers.
Our agents have been captured only twice and escaped once. Success rate: hopeful. Payment in advance, for obvious reasons.
Aged in the cellars of {hillock} until it complains. Rind may be harder than the plate. Rind may be the plate.
Printed on stone, never paper. Messages include 'it was already dead' and 'the chair was a gift'. Delivery by fast dwarf.
You will be seated on a crate of mugs. Crate may be sold mid-journey. Passengers may be sold mid-journey. We don't think so.
Available only to survivors, which keeps stock levels very manageable. Mug is spear-shaped. Do not drink from it.
Including beds, barrels, bins and grandparents. Stones carried one at a time, very slowly, by experienced haulers.
Updated yearly. Several entries now read 'gone'. Goblin section written in a hurry by a very nervous scholar.
